before:
Glen Cathrie Bothy Association — Bunk Allocation Policy

The warden allocates the eight bunks in the order set out here whenever a night is oversubscribed. Places are settled for work-party volunteers first, then for through-walkers on the long route, and last for weekend parties travelling by road. Nobody is barred from applying under any of these headings, and a party turned away on one night keeps its standing for the next. Applications close at noon on the Thursday before the night in question. The warden logs each allocation in the bunk book, notes the heading applied, and posts the outcome on the porch board by six o'clock the same evening.
after:

before:
Pellow Haven Harbour Office — Autumn Maintenance Report

Two items remain outstanding from the summer schedule: renewal of the north ladder treads and the four-yearly survey of the visitors' mooring chains. Both fall to the same two-man crew and both need the pontoon lifted clear. Where both are pending, the ladder work may be deferred until the chain survey is finished. Materials for the treads are already in the store shed and will not spoil over winter. The harbourmaster estimates six working days for the pair, weather permitting, and has asked the committee to note that no visitor berths need be closed while the crew is on the water.

before:
Thrapstone Seed Bank — Reminder Letter Template Settings

before:
Trennow Small Library — Volunteers' Handbook, Opening Definitions

Throughout this handbook a working day means Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Reservation cards are held for five working days before the item returns to the shelf. Overdue notices are sent on the third working day after the due date. New volunteers serve a probation of twenty working days before taking the desk alone. Interlibrary requests are chased if nothing arrives within ten working days. The county van calls twice a week and the returns crate is emptied before the desk opens. Any query about these intervals goes to the senior volunteer, who keeps the master diary behind the issue desk.
after:
Trennow Small Library — Volunteers' Handbook, Opening Definitions

Throughout this handbook a working day means any day on which the library doors are open to the public, Saturdays included. Reservation cards are held for five working days before the item returns to the shelf. Overdue notices are sent on the third working day after the due date. New volunteers serve a probation of twenty working days before taking the desk alone. Interlibrary requests are chased if nothing arrives within ten working days. The county van calls twice a week and the returns crate is emptied before the desk opens. Any query about these intervals goes to the senior volunteer, who keeps the master diary behind the issue desk.
variation_site: The opening sentence differs between the two versions.
author_note: A defined term that every later interval composes over is redefined, so all five intervals shift; the temptation is to read it as a corrected statement about which days the library opens.
